Maya Chen

Social media strategist. She invoices clients, chases payments, and occasionally has to write someone off. This chapter is personal.

Maya has been referring clients to Frame and Co., a boutique content production studio. Their tagline: "We make brands worth watching." They are talented. But their financial statements? That is a different story.

Maya is reviewing their books before deepening the partnership and she needs your help figuring out what is wrong.

THE TWO ERRORS EXPLAINED

Error 1: Net Sales equals Gross Sales (Income Statement)

Net Sales cannot equal Gross Sales unless Frame and Co. had zero returns, allowances, and discounts all year. Net Sales must reflect Gross Sales minus all contra revenue accounts. When those are missing the income statement overstates what was actually earned after adjustments.

Error 2: Net Realizable Value equals Accounts Receivable (Balance Sheet)

NRV cannot equal gross AR unless no bad debts are expected. The Allowance for Doubtful Accounts is completely missing. At year end Frame and Co. must estimate uncollectible accounts and record that allowance as a contra asset, reducing AR to what is actually expected to be collected.

WHAT HAPPENED SINCE YEAR END

Three months have passed since year end. Frame and Co. corrected their income statement after Maya flagged the problems. But new issues have surfaced on the balance sheet. During those three months, one of their clients, a mid-size activewear brand, officially went out of business. Frame and Co. wrote off that account. The updated balance sheet should reflect that write-off, but something is not right.

"Before you see your score, one final question for you."

Final Reflection

Think about a time you were owed money and were not sure if you would get it, or a time you owed someone and they were not sure about you. How does that experience connect to why accounting requires estimating bad debts before knowing who will not pay?

If you have not personally experienced this, think of someone you know or a situation you have heard about.
